name: Diné (Navajo)
notes: Southwestern US, Athabaskan-language (Na-Dené, Apachean branch) migrants into the Southwest, arrival timing genuinely contested (see claim_dine_migration_dating). "Navajo" derives from Spanish "Apaches de Nabajó," itself likely from a Tewa term for cultivated valley-land — not a pejorative exonym; "Navajo Nation" remains the tribal government’s own official current English name (reaffirmed by the Navajo Nation Council rejecting a 2017 proposal to rename it "Diné Nation"), while "Diné" ("the People") is preferred in cultural/self-referential and much recent scholarly usage. Significant Puebloan religious/cultural synthesis after the 1680 Pueblo Revolt and 1692 Spanish reconquest sent Puebloan refugees into Navajo country; the scale of this influence on Navajo cultural development has itself been argued as overstated in older models (Ronald H. Towner’s dendrochronological work).
